non_blocking: No paper found that contains the main result (pooled pick with NONE vs isolated verification on judge-unsolvable problems: more wrong picks in all-wrong pools AND more right picks in pools with a right answer, J not detectably different, pick near-uninformative). Search covered the required IDs plus listwise/pointwise judging, SDT/criterion-shift judge papers, none-of-the-above and abstention. Absence of a hit is not proof; searches were web-snippet based.

Cite arXiv 2610.08153 (Penalty-Framed No-Valid-Option MCQA): removes the correct option, lets models choose or ABSTAIN, and reports 'models still produce invalid forced-choice responses'. Closest unaddressed prior on forced choice when no option is valid; differs (MCQA, no isolated-verification contrast, no target-present hit rates, no solvability stratification). Related-work claim that only Wang 2025 covers NONE-style replacement should be softened.

Cite arXiv 2609.18204 (Beyond Accuracy: Procedural Traces Shift the Decision Criterion of LLM Overseers): applies signal detection theory to LLM judges and says 'AI auditors should be evaluated by their decision criterion and false-alarm behavior, alongside accuracy.' Precedent for the criterion-shift framing (different manipulation, shift toward rejection); the paper credits only the eyewitness literature (wixted2012field).

arXiv 2608.25937 (Candidate supply and answer selection shape the value of LLM judging) is correctly characterised: full text states 'All-wrong pools were' excluded from its stratified analyses; no overlap. 2611.00507 (Selecting or Solving) separates selection gain from verifier solving ability in video best-of-N; conceptually adjacent (judge competence vs selection), no all-wrong pools or criterion analysis. 2510.04087 and 2406.12319 are already cited and correctly distinguished. 2402.01349 is the Wang et al. paper already cited. Verified from arXiv abstracts.

NeurIPS 2026 poster 'Selected-Tail Reliability in Verifier-Guided Best-of-N Inference' (neurips.cc/virtual/2026/poster/155878): abstract-level only; theoretical selected-tail laws and Tail-Certified Compute Caps, no pooled-vs-isolated LLM judge experiment. Already cited as concurrent; fine.

Possibly cite arXiv 2610.02492 (pointwise vs bundled listwise judge protocol shifts acceptance-rate calibration: judges estimate '3.0%-97.9% of responses are acceptable') as protocol-dependent criterion evidence in listwise judging; I did not verify any all-wrong-pool result there.
